title: Etale ring maps: the conormal map of a finite presentation is an isomorphism
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $n\ge0$, $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring, and $\alpha:P\to S$ a surjective homomorphism of $R$-algebras whose kernel $J$ is a finitely generated ideal of $P$. The quotient $J/J^2$ is an $S=P/J$-module, and let $\bigoplus_{k=1}^nS\,\mathrm dx_k$ be the free $S$-module on symbols $\mathrm dx_1,\dots,\mathrm dx_n$. The map $\mathrm d:J/J^2\to\bigoplus_{k=1}^nS\,\mathrm dx_k$, $\mathrm d(g\bmod J^2)=\sum_{k=1}^n\alpha(\partial g/\partial x_k)\,\mathrm dx_k$ ($\partial/\partial x_k$ the formal partial derivatives of $P$ over $R$), is well defined and $S$-linear. Then the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ induced by $R\to S$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] if and only if $\mathrm d$ is bijective.

source.place: Definition Tag 00U1 (definition-etale, line 39245: $R\to S$ etale iff of finite presentation and $\NL_{S/R}$ quasi-isomorphic to zero, i.e. $H_1(\NL_{S/R})=0$ and $\Omega_{S/R}=0$), with the complex $\NL(\alpha):I/I^2\to\bigoplus S\,\mathrm dx_i$ of a presentation (text before Lemma Tag 00S1, line ~35190) and Lemma Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy, line 35274: $\NL(\alpha)\to\NL_{S/R}$ is a quasi-isomorphism); the cokernel of $\mathrm d$ is $\Omega_{S/R}$ by Lemma Tag 00RU (lemma-differential-seq); the comparison with etale morphisms of schemes by literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex Lemma Tag 02GJ (lemma-etale-characterize) and the remark in def-weil-etale-morphism (Stacks 02GI, 02GV, 02GE). This is the form of etaleness used in the proof of Algebra Lemma Tag 07RI ('The assumption is that the map d ... is an isomorphism').

proof.text: *$\mathrm d$ is well defined and $S$-linear.* The map $D:P\to\bigoplus_kS\,\mathrm dx_k$, $D(g)=\sum_k\alpha(\partial g/\partial x_k)\,\mathrm dx_k$, is additive and satisfies $D(hg)=\alpha(h)D(g)+\alpha(g)D(h)$ by the Leibniz rule for each $\partial/\partial x_k$. For $g\in J$ and $h\in P$ this gives $D(hg)=\alpha(h)D(g)$ since $\alpha(g)=0$; in particular $D(J^2)=0$ (take $h\in J$, so $\alpha(h)=0$). Hence $D|_J$ factors through $J/J^2$, and the resulting map $\mathrm d$ is linear for the $S=P/J$-module structure of $J/J^2$ ($\bar h\cdot(g\bmod J^2)=hg\bmod J^2$).

source.place: Algebra, text before Lemma Tag 00S1 (the complex NL(alpha): the class of f in I/I^2 maps to df (x) 1), line ~35190

proof.text: *The polynomial ring.* By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis], $\Omega_{P/R}$ is free with basis $\mathrm dx_1,\dots,\mathrm dx_n$, in particular a projective $P$-module, and $\mathrm dg=\sum_k(\partial g/\partial x_k)\,\mathrm dx_k$ for $g\in P$; by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-h1-cotangent-vanishing], $H_1(L_{P/R})=0$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Consequently $S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}$ is the free $S$-module with basis $1\otimes\mathrm dx_k$, and the $S$-linear isomorphism $\iota:S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}\to\bigoplus_kS\,\mathrm dx_k$, $1\otimes\mathrm dx_k\mapsto\mathrm dx_k$, sends $1\otimes\mathrm dg=\sum_k\alpha(\partial g/\partial x_k)\,(1\otimes\mathrm dx_k)$ to $\sum_k\alpha(\partial g/\partial x_k)\,\mathrm dx_k$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring, line 34306) and Lemma Tag 08Q1 (lemma-NL-polynomial-algebra, line 35391)

proof.text: *Kernel and cokernel of $\mathrm d$.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-quotient-smooth] with $A=R$, $B=P$ (its hypotheses $H_1(L_{P/R})=0$ and $\Omega_{P/R}$ projective hold by the previous step), $\mathfrak a=J$ and $C=P/J=S$ (with the $R$-algebra structure $R\to P\to S$, which is the given one since $\alpha$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras). It gives an exact sequence of $S$-modules $0\to H_1(L_{S/R})\to J/J^2\xrightarrow{\delta}S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{S/R}\to0$ with $\delta(g\bmod J^2)=1\otimes\mathrm dg$. By the previous step $\iota\circ\delta=\mathrm d$ with $\iota$ an isomorphism. Hence $\ker\mathrm d\cong H_1(L_{S/R})$ and $\operatorname{coker}\mathrm d\cong\Omega_{S/R}$, so $\mathrm d$ is bijective if and only if $H_1(L_{S/R})=0$ and $\Omega_{S/R}=0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL, Jacobi-Zariski sequence, line 35412) for R -> P -> S, with Lemma Tag 07BP (lemma-NL-surjection) and Lemma Tag 00RU (lemma-differential-seq, line 34103); this replaces the appeal to Lemma Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy) in the proof of Lemma Tag 00U9 (lemma-etale-standard-smooth, line 39265: 'As R -> S is etale we know that d : I/I^2 -> (+) S dx_i is an isomorphism')

proof.text: *Conclusion.* $S\cong P/J=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_m)$ for generators $g_1,\dots,g_m$ of the finitely generated ideal $J$, so $S$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] if and only if $S$ is finitely presented over $R$, $H_1(L_{S/R})=0$ and $\Omega_{S/R}=0$; the first condition holds, and by the previous step the other two together are equivalent to bijectivity of $\mathrm d$.

lean.statement: theorem etale_ring_map_conormal_criterion {R : Type u} {S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (n : ℕ) (α : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →ₐ[R] S) (hα : Function.Surjective α) (hfg : (RingHom.ker α.toRingHom).FG) : let J := RingHom.ker α.toRingHom let e := RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective hα letI : Module S J.Cotangent := Module.compHom J.Cotangent e.symm.toRingHom ∃ d : J.Cotangent →ₗ[S] (Fin n → S), (∀ (g : J) (i : Fin n), d (Ideal.toCotangent J g) i = α (MvPolynomial.pderiv i g.1)) ∧ (AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R S))) ↔ Function.Bijective d)
